runs.text: Leverage on the company's own measure rose over the year and has eased only slightly. Net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.50x in March 2025, 2.63x in September 2025, 3.07x in March 2026, 3.17x in June 2026 and 3.07x in September 2026, because net debt rose USD 521.3 million, or 11.66%, over the year while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 74.7 million, or 4.39%. Pro forma net debt for the October 2026 acquisition and the dividend expected on 2026-11-20 is not established, because neither amount is stated. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-8

Earnings are stabilising but not yet growing. Adjusted EBITDA fell 9.03% year on year in the first quarter of 2026 and 1.72% in the second, then rose 1.26% in the third, while operating margin fell from 5.45% in 2023 to 4.15% in the nine months to September 2026 and selling, general and administrative expense rose from 63.01% to 69.95% of gross profit. The mechanism is operating leverage: new-vehicle profit per unit keeps falling and same-store revenue is down, so each point of lost gross profit falls through to EBITDA, and a further decline of the size seen in the past year would lift leverage on the company's measure to 3.21x with net debt unchanged. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-18; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20

Interest cover is thin on total interest and ample on the corporate layer. Cash interest paid, which includes floor plan and financing-operations interest, was covered 2.79x by reported EBITDA over the trailing twelve months, but Adjusted EBITDA, which is struck after floor plan and financing interest, covered the remaining other interest expense of USD 271.0 million 6.00x. Floor plan interest expense rose 15.37% in the nine months, so higher rates and inventory feed straight into the numerator the company reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13

Cash flow quality is weak on a reported basis and the debt growth is mostly matched. Reported operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 204.9 million in the nine months because USD 831.4 million went into finance receivables and USD 555.0 million into inventory; finance receivables grew USD 823.5 million since the end of 2025 and financing-operations debt grew USD 784.3 million, so 95.24% of the added receivables was funded by debt that has no recourse beyond them. The remaining corporate-layer debt rose from USD 5,045.1 million to USD 5,176.8 million over the same period, which is where the buybacks of USD 624.5 million were funded. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-14

Financial policy is the main constraint. Repurchases of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 exceeded operating cash flow in both periods, the board added USD 500 million of repurchase authority in May 2026, and the chief executive became chairman in October 2026, so the check on distributions is weaker at the moment the company relies on borrowing. Covenant levels, the restricted-payments baskets and the guarantors are not in any supplied document, so whether distributions are limited by the debt documents is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

Liquidity is adequate and funding has been extended. Available funds were USD 1,440.7 million at 30 September 2026, 3.60x the USD 400.0 million of senior notes due 2027-12-15, which become due within twelve months at the end of 2026; the US Bank facility now runs to 2031-02-27, the Bank of Nova Scotia term facilities to 2029-03-18, the Mizuho warehouse to 2028-07-31 and the JPMorgan warehouse to 2027-12-09, and 82.98% of the senior notes mature in 2029 to 2031. Refinancing the 2029 notes at the 2030 notes' coupon, which is 162.5 bp higher, would add USD 13.0 million of annual interest, and the 2027 notes at 87.5 bp higher would add USD 3.5 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-17

Claims outside debt are modest. Operating lease liabilities were USD 765.3 million and finance leases of USD 112.4 million sit inside debt, the two defined benefit pension plans in the United Kingdom were funded with a surplus of USD 30.1 million at the end of 2025, the charge-back liability for early-terminated service contracts was USD 202.5 million with USD 112.8 million expected to be paid in 2026, and contract liabilities at September 2026 were USD 704.9 million, which are service obligations that unwind through delivery. The company reports no off-balance-sheet arrangements. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 97–98; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-21; calculation CALC-22; calculation CALC-23

runs.text: The first strength is a profit base weighted to service and finance. Aftersales and finance and insurance supplied 67.52% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026, so a fall in new-vehicle margin reduces earnings less than the vehicle mix alone would imply, which supports cash flow visibility and debt service through a vehicle-price cycle. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

The second strength is funding that is matched and extended. Inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against USD 4,509.2 million of financing-operations debt, and facility maturities were pushed to 2031, 2029 and 2028 in 2026, so near-term refinancing pressure on the large lines is low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14

The third strength is clean claims outside debt: pension plans were in surplus by USD 30.1 million at the end of 2025 and no off-balance-sheet arrangement is reported, so there is no hidden senior claim from pensions in the supplied evidence. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-21

The first weakness is distributions that exceed operating cash flow. Buybacks of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 were paid while operating cash flow was USD 356.7 million and an outflow of USD 204.9 million, which raises net debt and reduces headroom for the corporate layer's creditors. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is margin and growth. Operating margin fell to 4.15% and selling, general and administrative expense reached 69.95% of gross profit, while same-store revenue was 1.5% lower, so the earnings cushion over interest is narrowing and growth depends on acquisitions that add floor plan debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-19

The third weakness is that protections cannot be verified. Covenants, guarantors, collateral by instrument, ratings and board holdings are not in the supplied documents, and the chief executive is also chairman from 2026-10-19, so the checks that normally limit debt-funded distributions cannot be tested. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The group is an acquirer. It bought 56 stores in 2023, a far larger group in 2024 and 17 in 2025, selling 10 and 12 in the last two years, and in 2026 it has bought nine businesses in the nine months to September for USD 264.8 million of cash, with the announced annualized revenue of the stores acquired in each quarter at USD 425 million, USD 340 million and USD 150 million, plus USD 250 million for four stores in Memphis in October 2026. Two stores were sold in the third quarter with USD 115 million of annualized revenue, after three in the second quarter with USD 120 million. The October purchase is a subsequent event: neither its price nor its funding is stated, and it is not in any period figure. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-12

Two minority investments sit outside consolidation. Lithia holds 31.95% of Pinewood Technologies PLC, carried at fair value of USD 217.5 million against USD 177.2 million at the end of 2025, and 26.5% of Wheels, Inc. through Lithia Marubeni Mobility Holdings, carried at USD 221.0 million, with a dividend of USD 9.8 million received in the nine months. The Pinewood fair-value gain runs through other income and is excluded from the company's adjusted measures, so it does not support debt service. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

On debt, the only new senior notes in the period are USD 600.0 million of 5.500% notes due 2030, issued on 10 September 2025, redeemable from 1 October 2027 at a price that falls toward par, alongside the 2027, 2029 and 2031 notes of USD 2,350.0 million in total. In 2026 the company amended the US Bank syndicated facility on 27 February to a commitment of USD 6.5 billion maturing in 2031 with a lower used-vehicle floor plan margin of 1.20%, amended the Bank of Nova Scotia facility on the same date, extended the Mizuho warehouse commitment to 31 July 2028 at Daily Simple SOFR plus 0.825% on 30 September, and issued USD 1,520.2 million of non-recourse asset-backed notes in three transactions. The maturity extensions lengthen the funding profile; the use of the 2030 note proceeds is not stated in the sources. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–15; calculation CALC-11

Receipt of the credit agreement and the note indentures would make covenant headroom testable and would lift that limit; a further revision of reported figures beyond the 2024 correction would lower trust in the statements.

fields.value: The strongest case against reading the full-perimeter leverage as a creditor risk is asset matching: inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million, and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against financing-operations debt of USD 4,509.2 million, so most of the added debt is backed by assets that turn over or amortise. fields.value: Lithia sells new and used vehicles through franchised stores in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, and earns most of its profit from service, parts and finance and insurance. New vehicles are 49.70% of 2025 revenue but 20.39% of gross profit, while aftersales and finance and insurance together are 66.82% of gross profit, and the nine months to September 2026 show the same shape at 67.52%. That mix means vehicle margin compression, which cut new-vehicle gross profit per unit from USD 2,943 to USD 2,699 in the nine months, is cushioned by a service and finance base that is less tied to new-vehicle cycles.

fields.value: The company is concentrated by country and by franchise relationship. fields.value: Aftersales and finance income give earnings ballast, asset-matched funding limits the risk in the largest debt lines, and funding maturities now run to 2028 and beyond, but covenants, ratings and note guarantors are not established, so this is a limited view that rests on the company's own non-GAAP measures.

fields.value: Leverage on the company's own measure rose over the year and has eased only slightly. Net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.50x in March 2025, 2.63x in September 2025, 3.07x in March 2026, 3.17x in June 2026 and 3.07x in September 2026, because net debt rose USD 521.3 million, or 11.66%, over the year while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 74.7 million, or 4.39%. Pro forma net debt for the October 2026 acquisition and the dividend expected on 2026-11-20 is not established, because neither amount is stated.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are stabilising but not yet growing. Adjusted EBITDA fell 9.03% year on year in the first quarter of 2026 and 1.72% in the second, then rose 1.26% in the third, while operating margin fell from 5.45% in 2023 to 4.15% in the nine months to September 2026 and selling, general and administrative expense rose from 63.01% to 69.95% of gross profit. The mechanism is operating leverage: new-vehicle profit per unit keeps falling and same-store revenue is down, so each point of lost gross profit falls through to EBITDA, and a further decline of the size seen in the past year would lift leverage on the company's measure to 3.21x with net debt unchanged.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-18; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is thin on total interest and ample on the corporate layer. Cash interest paid, which includes floor plan and financing-operations interest, was covered 2.79x by reported EBITDA over the trailing twelve months, but Adjusted EBITDA, which is struck after floor plan and financing interest, covered the remaining other interest expense of USD 271.0 million 6.00x. Floor plan interest expense rose 15.37% in the nine months, so higher rates and inventory feed straight into the numerator the company reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality is weak on a reported basis and the debt growth is mostly matched. Reported operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 204.9 million in the nine months because USD 831.4 million went into finance receivables and USD 555.0 million into inventory; finance receivables grew USD 823.5 million since the end of 2025 and financing-operations debt grew USD 784.3 million, so 95.24% of the added receivables was funded by debt that has no recourse beyond them. The remaining corporate-layer debt rose from USD 5,045.1 million to USD 5,176.8 million over the same period, which is where the buybacks of USD 624.5 million were funded.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main constraint. Repurchases of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 exceeded operating cash flow in both periods, the board added USD 500 million of repurchase authority in May 2026, and the chief executive became chairman in October 2026, so the check on distributions is weaker at the moment the company relies on borrowing. Covenant levels, the restricted-payments baskets and the guarantors are not in any supplied document, so whether distributions are limited by the debt documents is not established.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and funding has been extended. Available funds were USD 1,440.7 million at 30 September 2026, 3.60x the USD 400.0 million of senior notes due 2027-12-15, which become due within twelve months at the end of 2026; the US Bank facility now runs to 2031-02-27, the Bank of Nova Scotia term facilities to 2029-03-18, the Mizuho warehouse to 2028-07-31 and the JPMorgan warehouse to 2027-12-09, and 82.98% of the senior notes mature in 2029 to 2031. Refinancing the 2029 notes at the 2030 notes' coupon, which is 162.5 bp higher, would add USD 13.0 million of annual interest, and the 2027 notes at 87.5 bp higher would add USD 3.5 million.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt are modest. Operating lease liabilities were USD 765.3 million and finance leases of USD 112.4 million sit inside debt, the two defined benefit pension plans in the United Kingdom were funded with a surplus of USD 30.1 million at the end of 2025, the charge-back liability for early-terminated service contracts was USD 202.5 million with USD 112.8 million expected to be paid in 2026, and contract liabilities at September 2026 were USD 704.9 million, which are service obligations that unwind through delivery. The company reports no off-balance-sheet arrangements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a weakening view is that the company's own leverage is flat since March 2026 at 3.07x, that the high point of 3.17x in June 2026 has already eased, that third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.26% on the year, that net credit losses on managed receivables fell to USD 47.8 million in the nine months from USD 54.1 million, and that 95.24% of the added receivables and most floor plan debt is matched by assets. That case would win if trailing Adjusted EBITDA turned up toward the USD 1,701.9 million of a year ago while repurchases slowed to within operating cash flow. It would lose if used-vehicle values or borrowing-base availability fell, because the matched debt would then be repaid faster than the assets convert, or if the executed credit agreement shows distribution limits that are already close to binding. On governance, the company kept a lead independent director when the chief executive became chairman, which is a partial check on the combined role.

fields.value: - The downside case applies the reported fall of 4.4% in trailing Adjusted EBITDA once more to unchanged net debt and is an anchored assumption, not a forecast, so the 3.21x outcome shows sensitivity and not a probable level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is a profit base weighted to service and finance. Aftersales and finance and insurance supplied 67.52% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026, so a fall in new-vehicle margin reduces earnings less than the vehicle mix alone would imply, which supports cash flow visibility and debt service through a vehicle-price cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is funding that is matched and extended. Inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against USD 4,509.2 million of financing-operations debt, and facility maturities were pushed to 2031, 2029 and 2028 in 2026, so near-term refinancing pressure on the large lines is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is clean claims outside debt: pension plans were in surplus by USD 30.1 million at the end of 2025 and no off-balance-sheet arrangement is reported, so there is no hidden senior claim from pensions in the supplied evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is distributions that exceed operating cash flow. Buybacks of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 were paid while operating cash flow was USD 356.7 million and an outflow of USD 204.9 million, which raises net debt and reduces headroom for the corporate layer's creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is margin and growth. Operating margin fell to 4.15% and selling, general and administrative expense reached 69.95% of gross profit, while same-store revenue was 1.5% lower, so the earnings cushion over interest is narrowing and growth depends on acquisitions that add floor plan debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is that protections cannot be verified. Covenants, guarantors, collateral by instrument, ratings and board holdings are not in the supplied documents, and the chief executive is also chairman from 2026-10-19, so the checks that normally limit debt-funded distributions cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant levels, restricted-payments baskets, guarantors and collateral by instrument are not established because the executed credit agreement and note indentures were not supplied; severity is high, because distribution capacity and liquidity usability cannot be tested, and the executed documents would close it.

fields.value: Credit ratings are not established because none is printed, although the annual report says the company monitors its credit ratings; severity is medium, and current ratings would close it.

fields.value: Year-end 2025 trailing Adjusted EBITDA is not printed, so leverage on the company's measure at 31 December 2025 is not established even though net debt of USD 4,864.1 million is; severity is medium, and the fourth-quarter 2025 release would close it.

fields.value: Pro forma net debt for the October 2026 acquisition and the dividend expected on 20 November 2026 is not established because the purchase price and dividend total are not stated; severity is low.
